meta.topic: Year 10 revision: energy, electricity and forces
meta.title: Revision Lesson
meta.subject: Physics

objectives: Recall and use the key energy equations from Year 10.
Apply circuit rules and electrical power equations.
Apply Newton's laws, momentum and stopping distances.

questions.q: State the units of energy and of power.
Write the equation that links potential difference, current and resistance.
In a series circuit, how does the current compare at different points?
Write Newton's second law as an equation.
What is the unit of momentum?
What is the frequency of the UK mains supply?

engage.title: LEARNING OBJECTIVES
engage.hook: Today: the big ideas from Year 10, then you show what you can do on your own.
engage.content:
1. Use the energy equations: kinetic, gravitational, elastic, heating, power and efficiency.
2. Use the circuit rules and V = IR, Q = It.
3. Use electrical power and explain the National Grid.
4. Use F = ma, momentum and stopping distances.

items: Energy is never created or destroyed, only transferred. Wasted energy is dissipated, usually by heating.
KE = {1/2}mv^2 · GPE = mgh · E_e = {1/2}ke^2 (e in m)
\Delta E = mc\Delta\theta · P = {E/t} · efficiency = {useful output/total input}

check.q: A 0.5 kg ball moves at 4 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy.
Calculate the energy to heat 2 kg of water by 5 °C (c = 4200 J/kg °C).
A motor takes in 200 J and gives out 80 J usefully. Calculate its efficiency.

items: Same current everywhere. Potential difference is shared. R_{total} = R_1 + R_2
Same potential difference across each branch. Branch currents add up. Total resistance is less than the smallest branch.

check.q: 12 V is across a 4 Ω resistor. Calculate the current.
A current of 0.5 A flows for 60 s. Calculate the charge.
Two 6 Ω resistors are in series. What is the total resistance?

items: P = IV · P = I^2R · E = QV · E = Pt
230 V, 50 Hz, alternating current. Live = brown, neutral = blue, earth = green and yellow.
Step-up transformers raise the potential difference, so the current is lower for the same power: less energy is wasted heating the cables.

check.q: A kettle on 230 V mains draws 10 A. Calculate its power.
Why does the National Grid use step-up transformers?
check.a: A higher p.d. means a lower current, so less energy is wasted heating the cables.

check.q: What colour is the live wire?

items: W = mg · F = ma · p = mv · F = ke · v^2 - u^2 = 2as
Distance-time: gradient = speed. Velocity-time: gradient = acceleration; area = distance.
Stopping distance = thinking distance + braking distance. Tiredness, alcohol and phones increase thinking distance; wet or icy roads and worn tyres or brakes increase braking distance.

check.q: Calculate the force needed to accelerate a 1200 kg car at 2 m/s^2.
Calculate the momentum of a 0.16 kg ball moving at 35 m/s.
Give two factors that increase braking distance.
check.a: Any two: wet or icy road; worn tyres; worn brakes; higher speed; greater mass.

developing.q: A 60 kg climber climbs 15 m. g = 9.8 N/kg. Calculate the gravitational potential energy gained.
A current of 2 A flows through a 6 Ω resistor. Calculate the potential difference across it.
A 900 kg car accelerates at 3 m/s^2. Calculate the resultant force on it.
Explain why the National Grid uses step-up transformers.
developing.a: They increase the potential difference, so the current is lower for the same power. A lower current wastes less energy heating the cables, so transmission is more efficient.

reaching.q: A 2.0 kW kettle heats 1.2 kg of water from 20 °C to 100 °C. c = 4200 J/kg °C. Calculate the energy needed and the time it takes, assuming no energy is wasted.
Two 10 Ω resistors are connected in parallel to a 6 V battery. Calculate the current from the battery.
reaching.a: Each branch: I = 6 \div 10 = 0.6 A; total = 0.6 + 0.6 = 1.2 A

reaching.q: A 1500 kg car travels at 20 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy and its momentum.
Explain how drinking alcohol and a wet road each affect the stopping distance of a car.
reaching.a: Alcohol increases reaction time, so the thinking distance increases. A wet road reduces friction between the tyres and the road, so the braking distance increases. Both increase the stopping distance.

mastering.q: A 0.05 kg toy is launched by a spring (k = 200 N/m) compressed by 0.04 m. Calculate the maximum launch speed, assuming all the elastic energy becomes kinetic energy.
A 3.0 kW heater runs for 20 minutes on the 230 V mains. Calculate the current and the charge that flows.
A 1200 kg car brakes from 25 m/s to rest in 50 m. Calculate the deceleration and the braking force.
mastering.a: 0 - 25^2 = 2 \times a \times 50, so a = -6.25 m/s^2 (deceleration 6.25 m/s^2); F = 1200 \times 6.25 = 7500 N
